literal: Geography Treatise III: Zhongjing Circuit
idiomatic: Geography Treatise III — Zhongjing Circuit

literal: Zhongjing, Dading Prefecture—in Yu's time it was Ying Prefecture; in Xia it belonged to Ji; in Zhou it lay within You's division.
idiomatic: Dading Prefecture at Zhongjing had been Ying Prefecture under Yu, Ji territory under Xia, and part of You under Zhou.

literal: Qin divided the realm into commanderies; this was Liaoxi.
idiomatic: When Qin organized the empire into commanderies, the region became Liaoxi.

literal: Under Han it was Xin'anping County.
idiomatic: In Han times it was Xin'anping County.

literal: At the end of Han the Bu Xi dwelt here; the domain ran a thousand li, with many great mountains and deep valleys—defiles enough to hold themselves secure.
idiomatic: In late Han the Bu Xi occupied the land, a thousand-li tract of high mountains and deep valleys whose passes let them stand on their own.

literal: Wei Wu-di on his northern campaign loosed troops in great battle; more than a hundred thousand surrendered and were sent away to Songmo.
idiomatic: On his northern campaign Cao Cao fought a major engagement; over one hundred thousand men surrendered and were removed to Songmo.

literal: Later the Tuoba clan, seizing the moment in Liaodong, set their headquarters here—south of the Raole River, north of the Wenyu River.
idiomatic: Later the Tuoba, exploiting turmoil in Liaodong, pitched their headquarters here between the Raole and Wenyu rivers.

literal: Tang Taizong campaigning against Goryeo halted his imperial progress here.
idiomatic: Tang Taizong campaigned against Goryeo and encamped here on imperial progress.

literal: Division chief Su Zhi followed the campaign with merit; Xi chief Kedou led the masses to submit inward, and the Raole Protectorate was set up for them.
idiomatic: Division chief Su Zhi distinguished himself on the campaign; Xi leader Kedou brought his people to submit, and the court established Raole Protectorate.

literal: After Xiantong the Khitan grew great and the Xi no longer dared resist.
idiomatic: After the Xiantong era the Khitan rose in power and the Xi ceased to resist.

literal: When the Founder established the state, the whole tribe became subjects.
idiomatic: When Taizu founded the dynasty, the entire tribe submitted.

literal: Shengzong once passed the bank of Qijin Mountain and the Tu River; gazing south at cloud vapors shaped like outer walls and towered gates, he discussed founding a capital.
idiomatic: Shengzong once traveled the Tu River below Qijin Mountain; seeing southern mists shaped like walls and gate-towers, he debated building a capital.

literal: Skilled craftsmen were chosen from Yan and Ji; construction was supervised two years—outer walls, palace quarters, towers, treasuries, markets and colonnades modeled on the Divine Capital's plan.
idiomatic: Craftsmen from Yan and Ji were recruited; for two years they built walls, palaces, towers, storehouses, and market arcades on the model of Luoyang.

literal: In Tonghe year 24 the Five Accounts Division presented the former Xi king's headquarters land.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 24 brought the Five Accounts Division's gift of the old Xi royal encampment grounds.

literal: Year 25 the city was walled and filled with Han households; it was styled Zhongjing, the prefecture called Dading.
idiomatic: In year 25 the walls rose and Han households settled it; the capital was named Zhongjing and the prefecture Dading.

literal: Within the Imperial City were ancestral temples and portrait halls to Emperor Jingzong and Empress Chengtian.
idiomatic: The Imperial City held ancestral shrines and portrait halls for Jingzong and Empress Chengtian.

literal: The city moat was damp and low; many wells were dug to drain it—people found this inconvenient.
idiomatic: The walled city sat in wet ground; numerous drainage wells were sunk, to the residents' inconvenience.

literal: Datong Hostel received Song envoys; Chaotian Hall received Silla envoys; Laibin Hall received Xia envoys.
idiomatic: The Datong hostel lodged Song missions, Chaotian Hall Silla missions, and Laibin Hall Xia missions.

literal: There were Qijin Mountain, Mayu Mountain, Twin Mountain, Song Mountain, and the Tu River.
idiomatic: Landmarks included Qijin, Mayu, Twin, and Song mountains and the Tu River.

literal: Ten prefectures, nine counties:
idiomatic: It governed ten prefectures and nine counties:

literal: Dading County.
idiomatic: Dading County.

literal: Former Bai Xi territory.
idiomatic: Ancient Bai Xi land.

literal: Captive households from various states were settled here.
idiomatic: Captives from many states were settled there.

literal: Changxing County.
idiomatic: Changxing County.

literal: Originally Han Bincong County.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Bincong County.

literal: Various tribal peoples were settled here.
idiomatic: Various tribal communities were placed there.

literal: Fushu County.
idiomatic: Fushu County.

literal: Originally Han Xin'anping territory; in Kaitai year 2 capital households were split off to establish it.
idiomatic: It was Han Xin'anping land; Kaitai year 2 carved out capital residents to found the county.

literal: Quannong County.
idiomatic: Quannong County.

literal: Originally Han Bincong County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Bincong County ground.

literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 detached capital households to create it.

literal: Wending County.
idiomatic: Wending County.

literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.
idiomatic: Established in Kaitai year 2 from capital households.

literal: Shengping County.
idiomatic: Shengping County.

literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.
idiomatic: Founded in Kaitai year 2 from capital residents.

literal: Guihua County.
idiomatic: Guihua County.

literal: Originally Han Liucheng County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Liucheng County land.

literal: Shenshui County.
idiomatic: Shenshui County.

literal: Originally Han Tuhe County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Tuhe County ground.

literal: Established in Kaitai year 2.
idiomatic: Created in Kaitai year 2.

literal: Jinyuan County.
idiomatic: Jinyuan County.

literal: Originally Tang Qingshan County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly within Tang Qingshan County.

literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 settled it with households drawn from the capital.

literal: En Prefecture, Huaide Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: En Prefecture—Huaide Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Xin'anping County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Xin'anping County land.

literal: Taizong established the prefecture.
idiomatic: Taizong created the prefecture.

literal: In Kaitai times Bohai households filled it.
idiomatic: During Kaitai Bohai households were settled there.

literal: First subordinate to Yongxing Palace, later to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: It first answered to Yongxing Palace, then to Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county: Enhua County.
idiomatic: One county: Enhua County.

literal: Established in Kaitai from Bohai households.
idiomatic: Settled in Kaitai with Bohai households.

literal: Hui Prefecture, Huihe Army, middle grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Hui Prefecture—Huihe Army, middle grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Tang Guiyi Prefecture territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Tang Guiyi Prefecture land.

literal: Taizu captured several hundred Han households below Tulu Mountain, founded a walled settlement, and set up the prefecture.
idiomatic: Taizu took several hundred Han households below Tulu Mountain, built a town, and established the prefecture.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing; governing one county: Huihe County.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing; one county, Huihe County.

literal: Shengzong moved Hui Prefecture households from Shangjing and gathered palace and camp registered households to settle them.
idiomatic: Shengzong relocated Hui households from Shangjing and enrolled palace and camp registers to populate it.

literal: Gao Prefecture, observation commissioner.
idiomatic: Gao Prefecture (observation commissioner).

literal: Tang Xin Prefecture territory.
idiomatic: Former Tang Xin Prefecture land.

literal: In Wansui Tongtian year 1 it was set up for the Khitan Shihuo division.
idiomatic: Wansui Tongtian year 1 placed the Khitan Shihuo division here.

literal: In Kaitai Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo and established Gao Prefecture with captives.
idiomatic: During Kaitai Shengzong's Goryeo campaign founded Gao Prefecture with war captives.

literal: There are Pingding Mountain and the Luan River.
idiomatic: It has Pingding Mountain and the Luan River.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county:
idiomatic: One county:

literal: Sanhan County—Chenhan was Fuyu, Bianhan Silla, Mahan Goryeo.
idiomatic: Sanhan County: Chenhan stood for Fuyu, Bianhan for Silla, Mahan for Goryeo.

literal: In Kaitai Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo and settled remnant people of the three states in the county.
idiomatic: During Kaitai Shengzong's Goryeo war placed survivors of the three Han states in the county.

literal: Households 5,000.
idiomatic: 5,000 households.

literal: Wu'an Prefecture, observation commissioner.
idiomatic: Wu'an Prefecture (observation commissioner).

literal: Tang Wo Prefecture territory.
idiomatic: Former Tang Wo Prefecture land.

literal: Taizu settled captured Han households below Muye Mountain, built a city to move them, styled Apricot Ridge New City.
idiomatic: Taizu placed Han captives below Muye Mountain, walled a new town called Apricot Ridge, and moved them in.

literal: Liaoxi households were added; it was renamed Xin Prefecture.
idiomatic: Liaoxi households swelled it and the seat was renamed Xin Prefecture.

literal: Tonghe year 8 received the present name.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 gave it the present name.

literal: At first a cishi; later promoted.
idiomatic: It began with a prefect and was later promoted.

literal: There are Huangbai Ridge, Liaoluo River, and Gemo River.
idiomatic: Features include Huangbai Ridge, Liaoluo River, and Gemo River.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county:
idiomatic: One county:

literal: Woye County.
idiomatic: Woye County.

literal: Li Prefecture, middle grade, observation commissioner.
idiomatic: Li Prefecture—middle grade, observation commissioner.

literal: Originally Zhongjing Fusu County.
idiomatic: Formerly Zhongjing's Fusu County.

literal: Tonghe year 26 set up as a cishi prefecture; Kaitai year 1 promoted.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 26 made it a prefecture with a cishi; Kaitai year 1 elevated it.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county:
idiomatic: One county:

literal: Fusu County.
idiomatic: Fusu County.

literal: At the end of Tang the Khitan grew strong, put the Xi to labor, and moved them to dwell on the Pipa River.
idiomatic: Late Tang saw the Khitan wax powerful, conscript Xi labor, and resettle them on the Pipa River.

literal: Established as a county in Tonghe year 4.
idiomatic: Made a county in Tonghe year 4.

literal: First subordinate to Zhangmin Palace, then reassigned to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: It first belonged to Zhangmin Palace, then to Zhongjing.

literal: Later a prefecture was set up, still subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: A prefecture followed, still under Zhongjing.

literal: Yu Prefecture, Gaoping Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Yu Prefecture—Gaoping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Linyu County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Linyu County land.

literal: Later subordinate to Youbeiping Licheng County.
idiomatic: Later it fell under Youbeiping's Licheng County.

literal: Tang Zai Chu year 2 split Shen Prefecture to set up Li Prefecture for Mohe tribes; later the Xi seized it.
idiomatic: In Tang Zai Chu year 2 Li Prefecture was carved from Shen to settle Mohe tribes, until the Xi took it.

literal: Taizong on the southern campaign: the Horizontal Account Jieli settled captured Zhen Prefecture households and founded the prefecture; in Kaitai it was absorbed and abolished.
idiomatic: On his southern campaign Taizong's Horizontal Account Jieli placed Zhen captives here; Kaitai absorbed and abolished the prefecture.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing two counties:
idiomatic: Two counties:

literal: Hezhong County.
idiomatic: Hezhong County.

literal: Originally Xinli County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Xinli County land.

literal: Yonghe County.
idiomatic: Yonghe County.

literal: Originally Han Changcheng County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Changcheng County ground.

literal: Established in Tonghe year 22.
idiomatic: Founded in Tonghe year 22.

literal: Ze Prefecture, Guangji Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Ze Prefecture—Guangji Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Tuyin County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Tuyin County land.

literal: Taizu captured Wei Prefecture households, set up a stockade, and mined and smelted Xianhe silver works.
idiomatic: Taizu took Wei Prefecture captives, founded a stockade, and worked the Xianhe silver mines.

literal: Subordinate to the Zhongjing regent's office.
idiomatic: It answered to the Zhongjing regent.

literal: Ze Prefecture was set up in Kaitai.
idiomatic: Kaitai established Ze Prefecture.

literal: There are Songting Pass, Spirit Mountain, Jiugong Ridge, Shizi Ridge, the Luo River, and the Sa River.
idiomatic: Landmarks include Songting Pass, Spirit Mountain, Jiugong and Shizi ridges, the Luo River, and the Sa River.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing two counties:
idiomatic: Two counties:

literal: Shenshan County.
idiomatic: Shenshan County.

literal: Spirit Mountain lies to the southwest.
idiomatic: Spirit Mountain stands in the southwest.

literal: Luanhe County.
idiomatic: Luanhe County.

literal: Originally Han Xuwu County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Xuwu County land.

literal: Subordinate to Yongxing Palace.
idiomatic: Under Yongxing Palace.

literal: Bei'an Prefecture, Xinghua Army, upper grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Bei'an Prefecture—Xinghua Army, upper grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Nuqi County territory, belonging to Shanggu Commandery.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Nuqi County in Shanggu Commandery.

literal: Under Jin it was seized by Feng Ba.
idiomatic: Jin times saw Feng Ba take it.

literal: Under Tang it was western territory of the Xi princely mansion.
idiomatic: Tang made it the Xi princely house's western domain.

literal: Shengzong settled Han households to establish Bei'an Prefecture.
idiomatic: Shengzong placed Han households and founded Bei'an Prefecture.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county: Xinghua County.
idiomatic: One county: Xinghua County.

literal: Originally Han Qieju County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Qieju County land.

literal: Tan Prefecture, Guangrun Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Tan Prefecture—Guangrun Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Longshan County of Zhongjing; the prefecture was set up in Kaitai and remained under Zhongjing.
idiomatic: It was Zhongjing's Longshan County; Kaitai made it a prefecture still under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county: Longshan County.
idiomatic: One county: Longshan County.

literal: Originally Han Jiaoli County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Jiaoli County ground.

literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from Xijia Stockade.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 founded it from Xijia Stockade.

literal: Songshan Prefecture, Sheng'an territory, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Songshan Prefecture—Sheng'an territory, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Established in Kaitai.
idiomatic: Created in Kaitai.

literal: Abolished in Tonghe year 8, then restored.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 abolished it; later it was restored.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county:
idiomatic: One county:

literal: Songshan County.
idiomatic: Songshan County.

literal: Originally Han Wencheng County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Wencheng County land.

literal: Bordering Songmo, a merchant crossroads.
idiomatic: On the Songmo frontier, a hub of trade.

literal: Established as a county in Kaitai year 2.
idiomatic: Made a county in Kaitai year 2.

literal: There is the Song Mountain stream.
idiomatic: The Song Mountain river runs through it.

literal: Song minister Wang Zeng's Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan says: leaving Yanjing's north gate, one reaches Wangjing Hostel.
idiomatic: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: from Yanjing's north gate to Wangjing Hostel,

literal: fifty li to Shun Prefecture.
idiomatic: fifty li to Shun Prefecture;

literal: seventy li to Tan Prefecture, gradually entering mountains.
idiomatic: seventy li to Tan Prefecture as the road climbs into hills;

literal: fifty li to Jingou Hostel.
idiomatic: another fifty li reaches Jingou Hostel.

literal: Approaching the hostel, the river plain opens wide—called the Jingou shoals.
idiomatic: Near the hostel the valley floor widens into what they call the Jingou flats.

literal: From here one enters the mountains, winding up steep paths; there are no more mile markers—only days on horseback estimate the distance.
idiomatic: Beyond lies twisting mountain grades without mileposts; travelers count days on horseback to reckon distance.

literal: Ninety li to Gubeikou; steep cliffs on both sides barely admit a cart track.
idiomatic: Ninety li brings Gubeikou, where cliffs on both sides admit only a single cart track.

literal: Crossing Desheng Ridge with its layered switchbacks—folk name Homesick Ridge—eighty li to Xin Hostel.
idiomatic: Desheng Ridge's switchbacks, known as Homesick Ridge, lead eighty li to Xin Hostel.

literal: Passing Diaoke Ridge and Pianqiang Ridge, forty li to Wolai Hostel.
idiomatic: Past Diaoke and Pianqiang ridges, forty li to the Reclining Tathagata Hostel.

literal: Crossing the Wuluan River—with Luan Prefecture to the east—then Modou Ridge, also called Duyun Ridge and Qincai Ridge; seventy li to Liuhe Hostel.
idiomatic: The Wuluan River is crossed with Luan Prefecture eastward; Modou Ridge, alias Duyun and Qincai ridges, lies seventy li before Liuhe Hostel.

literal: Songting Ridge is very precipitous; seventy li to the Forging Tribes Hostel.
idiomatic: Songting Ridge is sheer; seventy li farther stands the Forging Tribes Hostel.

literal: Southeast fifty li to Niushan Hostel.
idiomatic: Fifty li southeast to Niushan Hostel.

literal: Eighty li to Lu'er Gorge Hostel.
idiomatic: Eighty li to Deer Gorge Hostel.

literal: Crossing Hamo Ridge, ninety li to Tiejiang Hostel.
idiomatic: Over Hamo Ridge, ninety li to Iron-Slurry Hostel.

literal: Crossing Shizi Ridge, from here gradually leaving the mountains, seventy li to Fugu Hostel.
idiomatic: Shizi Ridge passed, the road slowly descends from the hills; seventy li to Fugu Hostel.

literal: Eighty li to Tongtian Hostel, twenty li to Zhongjing, Dading Prefecture.
idiomatic: Eighty li to Tongtian Hostel, then twenty li to Zhongjing at Dading Prefecture.

literal: The walls are low and small; the circuit barely four li square.
idiomatic: Walls are low and the city circuit scarcely four li around.

literal: Gates are only layered roofs, without tower-gate construction.
idiomatic: Gatehouses are stacked roofs without barbican towers.

literal: The south gate is called Zhuxia; within the gate connected walking corridors and many ward gates.
idiomatic: The south gate Zhuxia opens on covered walkways and many lane gates.

literal: There are also four market towers: called Tianfang, Daqu, Tonghuan, and Wangque.
idiomatic: Four market towers stand: Tianfang, Daqu, Tonghuan, and Wangque.

literal: Next one reaches Datong Hostel.
idiomatic: Farther on lies Datong Hostel.

literal: Its gate due north is called Yangde and Changge.
idiomatic: Its north-facing gate bears the names Yangde and Changge.

literal: Within the city on a hillock in the southwest corner is a temple.
idiomatic: A temple crowns a southwest hill inside the walls.

literal: South of the city are gardens, a place for banquets and archery.
idiomatic: South of the walls lie gardens used for feasts and archery.

literal: From passing Gubeikou, inhabitants live in thatched huts and plank houses and farm, but there is no mulberry or catalpa;
idiomatic: Beyond Gubeikou people dwell in thatch huts and plank houses and till fields, yet plant no mulberry or catalpa;

literal: all planting is on ridge crests, lest blown sand bury the crops.
idiomatic: crops are sown on ridge tops for fear windblown sand would bury them.

literal: In the mountains tall pines grow dense; deep valleys sometimes show pastured cattle, horses, and camels—many blue sheep and yellow swine.
idiomatic: Mountains hold thick pine; valleys often show cattle, horses, and camels, with many blue sheep and yellow hogs.

literal: Cheng Prefecture, Xingfu Army, military commission.
idiomatic: Cheng Prefecture—Xingfu Army, military commissioner.

literal: The Jin state's Senior Princess established it with dowry households; the army was called Changqing, subordinate to Shangjing.
idiomatic: The Jin Senior Princess founded it with dowry households under the Changqing army, subordinate to Shangjing.

literal: The army name was changed again.
idiomatic: The army designation was later renamed.

literal: Governing one county: Tongchang County.
idiomatic: One county: Tongchang County.

literal: Xingzhong Prefecture.
idiomatic: Xingzhong Prefecture.

literal: Originally Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.
idiomatic: Formerly Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army), military commissioner.

literal: The ancient Guzhu state.
idiomatic: Land of ancient Guzhu.

literal: Han Liucheng County territory.
idiomatic: Han Liucheng County ground.

literal: Murong Huang, taking the land north of Liucheng and south of Long Mountain as a place of fortune and virtue, built Long City, erected palaces and temples, changed Liucheng to Longcheng County, moved the capital, and styled it Helong Palace.
idiomatic: Murong Huang deemed the tract between Liucheng and Long Mountain auspicious, built Long City with palaces and shrines, renamed Liucheng Longcheng County, moved the capital, and called it Helong Palace.

literal: Murong Chui dwelt there again; later it was destroyed by Northern Yan.
idiomatic: Murong Chui returned there; Northern Yan later destroyed it.

literal: Northern Wei took it as Liaoxi Commandery.
idiomatic: Northern Wei made it Liaoxi Commandery.

literal: Sui pacified Gao Baoning and set up Ying Prefecture.
idiomatic: Sui subdued Gao Baoning and established Ying Prefecture.

literal: Emperor Yang abolished the prefecture and set up Liucheng Commandery.
idiomatic: Sui Yang-di abolished the prefecture for Liucheng Commandery.

literal: Early Tang Wude changed it to Ying Prefecture chief commandery, soon a protectorate headquarters.
idiomatic: Early Tang Wude made it Ying chief command, soon a protectorate seat.

literal: In Wansui Tongtian it fell to Li Wanrong.
idiomatic: Wansui Tongtian saw it lost to Li Wanrong.

literal: Early Shenlong moved the headquarters to Youzhou.
idiomatic: Early Shenlong shifted the seat to Youzhou.

literal: Kaiyuan year 4 restored administration at Liucheng.
idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 4 returned government to Liucheng.

literal: Year 8 it moved west to Yuyang.
idiomatic: Year 8 the seat moved west to Yuyang.

literal: Year 10 it returned to Liucheng.
idiomatic: Year 10 brought it back to Liucheng.

literal: Later the Xi seized it.
idiomatic: The Xi later held it.

literal: Taizu pacified the Xi and captured Yan households; intending to build a city, he ordered Han Zhifang to choose the site.
idiomatic: Taizu subdued the Xi, took Yan captives, and charged Han Zhifang to choose a city site.

literal: Liucheng was then repaired and styled Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.
idiomatic: Liucheng was rebuilt as Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army) with a military commissioner.

literal: In Tonghe times the frontier commission of Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan five prefectures was set up.
idiomatic: Tonghe created a frontier commission over Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan prefectures.

literal: Soon the commission was abolished; it was subordinate to Jiqing Palace.
idiomatic: The commission was soon dropped and the seat joined Jiqing Palace.

literal: Later it belonged to Xingsheng Palace.
idiomatic: Later it passed to Xingsheng Palace.

literal: Chongxi year 10 it was promoted to Xingzhong Prefecture.
idiomatic: Chongxi year 10 elevated it to Xingzhong Prefecture.

literal: There are Great Huashan, Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk-fragrance Cliff—with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's carved stone—Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.
idiomatic: It boasts Great and Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk Cliff with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's inscription, Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.

literal: Two prefectures, four counties:
idiomatic: It governed two prefectures and four counties:

literal: Xingzhong County.
idiomatic: Xingzhong County.

literal: Originally Han Liucheng County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Liucheng County land.

literal: Taizu plundered Han households to dwell here and built Bacheng County.
idiomatic: Taizu settled plundered Han households and founded Bacheng County.

literal: In Chongxi the prefecture was set up and the name changed.
idiomatic: Chongxi established the prefecture and renamed the county.

literal: Yingqiu County.
idiomatic: Yingqiu County.

literal: Split off from Bacheng.
idiomatic: Carved from Bacheng.

literal: Xianglei County.
idiomatic: Xianglei County.

literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from Maiwu River.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 founded it on the Maiwu River.

literal: First subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: First under Zhongjing.

literal: Later subordinate.
idiomatic: Later subordinate.

literal: Lüshan County.
idiomatic: Lüshan County.

literal: Originally Han Qielü County.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Qielü County.

idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 created it from the Luo Family Army.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing, later subordinate.
idiomatic: First under Zhongjing, later under the prefecture.

literal: An'de Prefecture, Huaping Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: An'de Prefecture—Huaping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Set up from Ba Prefecture's An'de County; came under this prefecture.
idiomatic: Created from Ba's An'de County and attached here.

literal: Governing one county: An'de County.
idiomatic: One county: An'de County.

literal: Tonghe year 8 split households from southeast Bacheng, Long Mountain, and Tuhe borders to establish it.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 settled households from southeast Bacheng and the Long Mountain and Tuhe marches.

literal: First subordinate to Qian Prefecture, then to Ba Prefecture; when the prefecture was set up it came under this seat.
idiomatic: It first belonged to Qian, then Ba; establishing the prefecture brought it here.

literal: Qian Prefecture, Fuchang Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Qian Prefecture—Fuchang Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Liaoxi Commandery territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Liaoxi Commandery land.

literal: Taizu pacified Bohai and settled captives here, subordinate to the Blackwater River commissioner.
idiomatic: Taizu conquered Bohai, placed captives here under the Blackwater River commissioner.

literal: Emperor An established the prefecture and added Han households split from Yi and Ba prefectures.
idiomatic: Emperor An founded the prefecture and augmented it with Han households from Yi and Ba.

literal: First subordinate to Yongxing Palace, then to Zhongjing; after the prefecture was set up it came under this seat.
idiomatic: It passed from Yongxing Palace to Zhongjing, then to Xingzhong when that prefecture rose.

literal: Governing one county: Shengji County.
idiomatic: One county: Shengji County.

idiomatic: After Bohai's conquest, Xing Prefecture's Shengji captives were settled and the county founded.

literal: Yi Prefecture, Chongyi Army, upper grade, military commission.
idiomatic: Yi Prefecture—Chongyi Army, upper grade, military commissioner.

literal: Originally Liaoxi Lei County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Liaoxi Lei County land.

literal: The Dongdan king hunted here every autumn.
idiomatic: The Dongdan king autumn-hunted here each year.

literal: Xingzong established the prefecture with captives from Ding Prefecture.
